rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord ending a tenancy or not renewing a lease must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice to the City through its portal. Violations do not halt the eviction.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with every notice to quit/non-renewal; copy to City
rules.quoted_span: The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit
rules.effective_date_note: Tenant FAQ states the HSNA becomes effective November 6, 2020; ordinance passed October 2020.
rules.exemptions: Residences in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.
rules.penalty: 1st offense: warning; 2nd and subsequent: $300 per day (enforced by ISD).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy.

unverifiable_exemptions: residence in hospital, skilled nursing or health facility
non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facility

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb 2017)
rules.requirement: Housing providers with DND funding/land or BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units may not use a blanket ban on applicants with arrests or convictions and must review case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, convictions with judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old (with exceptions), and may not use credit scores to approve or deny applications.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-history bans; no non-conviction arrests, juvenile records, or convictions >5 years old; no credit scores
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
citation_aliases: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.quoted_span: Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion programs, and similar non-convictions.
rules.effective_date_note: Only the February 2017 policy date is given.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies only to housing providers receiving DND funding or land, or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where a conviction directly relates to the housing sought or poses unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others, or to current criminal behavior. Conflicting federal or state law preempts it.
rules.interaction: Federal or state law imposing a conflicting criminal history requirement preempts this policy.
rules.conflict_note: Funding-conditioned policy under which providers 'agree' to its terms, not a general ordinance; enforcement unclear.

requires_unknown_facts: property receives DND funding or land, or has income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy

no_rule_findings.finding: State law bars municipalities from enacting or enforcing rent control, so Boston has no local rent cap.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

no_rule_findings.finding: Home-rule petition H.3744 to let Boston implement rent stabilization was not enacted; it was accompanied by a study order (H5035) on 9/9/2024.

parsed.notes: Merged HSNA candidates c15 and c16 into one record. I dropped n1: H.3744 did not become law, and Boston's HSNA is a notice rule, not a just-cause limit. I did not add a Boston source-of-income rule because the document gives no code citation. The documents provided have no Boston-level rules or findings for security deposits, application fees or algorithmic rent setting.
